plan.title: Liver treated vs control DE with power caveat (n=3)
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is a single-batch, unpaired 3-vs-3 human liver bulk RNA-seq comparison (drug-treated vs control) from Salmon gene-level counts (12000 genes x 6 samples of the 7-column counts file; 1 column is the gene symbol). Given only 3 replicates per group, the plan follows the grounded procedure for small-n bulk RNA-seq DE: (1) QC on sample structure before any test, to catch a mislabeled or outlier sample that would be fatal at n=3; (2) a minimal count pre-filter, leaving true significance selection to DESeq2's independent filtering; (3) DESeq2 Wald test with median-of-ratios normalization and apeglm shrinkage as the primary model, with an edgeR quasi-likelihood cross-check run on the same filtered counts and design as a robustness check — the intersection of the two gene sets is reported as the high-confidence DE set, and single-method-only genes are reported separately; (4) BH-adjusted significance at alpha=0.05 with independent filtering, no ad hoc p-value or fold-change-only cutoffs; (5) preranked GSEA (fgsea) against MSigDB Hallmark using the DESeq2 Wald statistic as the ranking metric, only if a human Hallmark gene set collection is confirmed present in the environment; (6) a final report that states, in addition to the gene tables, the explicit low-power caveat for n=3 (few true positives detected, most with large effect sizes, and an untested gene is not evidence of no change), NA-p-value counts from Cook's-distance outlier flags, and full method/version/threshold reporting per the grounded standard. Reference level for the condition factor is set explicitly to control (from metadata.csv) so a positive log2FC means higher expression in treated.

steps.method: keep genes with >=10 counts in >=3 samples (smallest group size)
fgsea preranked GSEA on Wald statistic, MSigDB Hallmark
summary report with method, versions, design, thresholds, n_tested, n_de, overlap of DESeq2/edgeR, power caveat
